subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `openclaw cron run` permanently be a non-consuming operator/verification operation for every run mode, with scheduler-owned state changes reserved to timer and on-exit watcher internals?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility contract change for manual `due` and `force` calls, not a mechanical test or implementation question; current source evidence supports the design but cannot establish owner acceptance.

options.title: Adopt operator-only public runs
options.body: Confirm that public manual runs preserve scheduled state and one-shot consumption, while only timer and the concrete on-exit watcher own scheduler finalization.

options.title: Preserve a public consuming mode
options.body: Require an explicitly designed, documented, and compatibility-tested public API for operators who intentionally need a manual run to consume scheduler state.

recommendation.title: Adopt operator-only public runs
recommendation.body: Confirm that public manual runs preserve scheduled state and one-shot consumption, while only timer and the concrete on-exit watcher own scheduler finalization.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron scheduling-state work covers the same due-slot and next-run invariants.
